title: Procedural Heat Haze Distortion Effect
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a procedural heat haze distortion post-processing effect with full interactive controls.

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a scene with a perspective camera at position (0, 2, 8) looking at origin
- Add a ground plane (20x20) with a checkerboard texture (generated procedurally via canvas) so distortion is clearly visible
- Place 3 colored boxes (red, green, blue) at positions (-2,1,0), (0,1,0), (2,1,0) respectively, each 1x2x1
- Add a directional light from (5,10,5) and ambient light
- Add a bright orange emissive plane at y=0, z=-2 representing the 'heat source' (4x0.1x1)

SHADER IMPLEMENTATION:
- Implement heat haze as a full-screen post-processing effect using THREE.ShaderPass or custom render-to-texture pipeline
- The distortion shader must use a noise function (simplex or perlin, implemented in GLSL) to offset UV coordinates
- Distortion should be stronger near the bottom of the screen (simulating ground-level heat) controlled by a vertical gradient
- The distortion must animate over time using a uniform 'uTime' incremented each frame
- Key shader uniforms: uTime (float), uDistortionStrength (float, 0.0-0.1, default 0.03), uFrequency (float, 1.0-20.0, default 8.0), uSpeed (float, 0.1-5.0, default 1.5), uVerticalFade (float, 0.0-1.0, default 0.7), uEnabled (bool, default true)

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Press '1' to decrease distortion strength by 0.005 (clamp to 0.0 min)
- Press '2' to increase distortion strength by 0.005 (clamp to 0.1 max)
- Press '3' to decrease frequency by 1.0 (clamp to 1.0 min)
- Press '4' to increase frequency by 1.0 (clamp to 20.0 max)
- Press '5' to decrease speed by 0.2 (clamp to 0.1 min)
- Press '6' to increase speed by 0.2 (clamp to 5.0 max)
- Press 'H' to toggle the heat haze effect on/off (uEnabled)
- Press 'R' to reset all parameters to defaults
- Press 'V' to cycle vertical fade through presets: [0.0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0] wrapping around

HUD/UI:
- Display a DOM overlay panel (id='hud') in top-left showing current values:
  - 'Strength: X.XXX'
  - 'Frequency: X.X'
  - 'Speed: X.X'
  - 'Vertical Fade: X.X'
  - 'Effect: ON/OFF'
  - 'Frame: NNNN'

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - enabled: boolean (whether effect is active)
  - distortionStrength: number (current strength value)
  - frequency: number (current frequency)
  - speed: number (current speed)
  - verticalFade: number (current vertical fade)
  - verticalFadeIndex: number (index into presets array)
  - time: number (accumulated uTime value)
  - frame: number (frame counter)
  - fps: number (approximate frames per second)
  - boxCount: number (should be 3)
  - shaderCompiled: boolean (true if shader compiled without errors)
  - renderTargetWidth: number (render target resolution width)
  - renderTargetHeight: number (render target resolution height)

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:
- Use EffectComposer pattern or manual two-pass rendering (render scene to texture, then apply distortion shader as fullscreen quad)
- The noise function in the fragment shader must produce smooth, continuous distortion
- Ensure render targets resize with window
- Animation loop must use requestAnimationFrame
- All numerical state values must be NaN-free at all times
physics_constraints: Distortion strength must remain in [0.0, 0.1], frequency in [1.0, 20.0], speed in [0.1, 5.0], vertical fade in [0.0, 1.0]. Time must monotonically increase when effect is enabled. Frame counter must monotonically increase. All shader uniforms must be finite numbers (no NaN/Infinity).
